While we are adding talented employees to our ranks and licensing Groq's IP, we are not acquiring Groq as a company" Simon Edwards is Groq's new CEO. He was previously Groq's Chief Financial Officer Nvidia plans to integrate Groq's processors into their existing "AI factory architecture" rather than manufacture standalone Groq chips https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/nvidia-buys-ai-chip-startup-groqs-assets-for-usd20-billion-in-the-companys-biggest-deal-ever-transaction-includes-acquihires-of-key-groq-employees-including-ceo https://groq.com/newsroom/groq-and-nvidia-enter-non-exclusive-inference-technology-licensing-agreement-to-accelerate-ai-inference-at-global-scale Groq's Tensor Streaming Processors (TSP) are designed in-house and manufactured using multiple foundries (not TSMC); The chip is massive at 725mm² and uses primarily on-chip SRAM (230MB) instead of external memory like HBM Current Generation (LPU v1, 14nm): Manufactured by GlobalFoundries in upstate New York Next Generation (LPU v2, 4nm): Groq selected Samsung Foundry at Taylor, Texas facility While Groq doesn't use TSMC or Taiwan-based manufacturing, both GlobalFoundries and Samsung foundries do use ASML's lithography equipment for chip fabrication

slides.title: AI Updates AI Model Quality Saturation AI Model
slides.text: AI Updates AI Model Quality Saturation AI Model improvements no longer matter much for most users Once models reach "PhD-level" capability, speed and integration become more valuable than raw intelligence gains Reasoning models are slow. Users prefer fast good enough models Users want models to integrate with common apps (Gmail, ...) The immediate battle is about embedding AI into existing workflows rather than making smarter models https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwpxEFpdlYo Importance of Continual learning Continual learning enables AI agents to update their knowledge incrementally from new experiences without forgetting previously learned information, addressing the critical problem of "catastrophic forgetting" where traditional models lose old knowledge when learning new tasks This capability is essential for enterprise AI because r eal-world environments constantly change - business processes evolve, customer behaviors shift, policies update, and new edge cases emerge - requiring agents that adapt continuously rather than remaining frozen at their initial training state Without continual learning, organizations face expensive retraining cycles, system downtime, and agents that quickly become outdated , Continually learning agents reduce operational overhead while improving performance organically over time Continual learning approach combines incremental updates that preserve existing knowledge with the ability to absorb new rules, exceptions, and workflows, making agents behave more like real team members who improve with experience rather than static tools requiring quarterly resets As foundation models grow larger and retraining becomes prohibitively expensive , continual learning through memory-augmented architectures and token-space updates offers a sustainable path to adaptive, evolving systems that can transfer knowledge across model generations while maintaining durable improvements https://beam.ai/agentic-insights/what-is-continual-learning-(and-why-it-powers-self-learning-ai-agents) https://www.letta.com/blog/continual-learning https://www.xoriant.com/thought-leadership/article/agentic-ai-and-continuous-learning-creating-ever-evolving-systems https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.03320 https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/continual-learning Ph.D. Quality Slow Inference Expensive Re-Training Fast Inference Long Context Multi-Step Continual Learning

slides.title: Catastrophic forgetting Catastrophic forgetting - the model loses
slides.text: Catastrophic forgetting Catastrophic forgetting - the model loses performance on old tasks/knowledge after being trained on new data It is a tendency of a model to “overwrite” previously acquired capabilities when adapted to new instructions In continual or sequential learning, catastrophic forgetting (also called catastrophic interference) is the abrupt degradation of performance on earlier tasks when the model is trained on new tasks using the same parameters This happens because gradient updates for the new data push weights into regions that no longer support the old behaviors Unlike ordinary gradual forgetting in humans, this effect in neural nets can be sudden and severe a model that previously performed well on task A can almost completely fail after being optimized for task B if no precautions are taken For long‑lived agents that need continual learning, the ability to integrate new information without harming old skills becomes a core requirement, making catastrophic forgetting a central research and engineering concern Mitigation strategies: regularization or parameter‑isolation methods (e.g., constraining updates, using separate low‑rank adapters, or orthogonal subspaces for new tasks) replay methods that mix a small buffer of old-task data with new data selective or frozen-parameter fine‑tuning rather than updating the entire model

slides.title: Network Training & Fine-Tuning Neural network training follows
slides.text: Network Training & Fine-Tuning Neural network training follows surprisingly low-dimensional paths through high-dimensional spaces, like water carving riverbeds Despite vast differences in architecture, optimization methods, or initialization, networks converge along similar manifolds during training The iterative process - predicting, computing loss, and optimizing across epochs - creates well-worn routes through parameter space. Networks starting from completely different points, even those initially trained on random labels, quickly merge their trajectories toward true labels along shared paths. Stochastic gradient descent with nonlinear activations helps networks escape local minima that would trap traditional gradient descent, similar to water navigating obstacles while flowing downward This reveals how training naturally discovers efficient routes through overwhelmingly complex optimization landscapes. Modern fine-tuning techniques like LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) use a "two-worker" approach . The "old worker" is the frozen pre-trained base model , preserving knowledge from expensive training on massive datasets. The "baby worker" consists of small trainable adapter matrices learning from task-specific data. These workers operate in parallel at each transformer layer - the base model is typically quantized for memory efficiency while remaining frozen, and lightweight adapters capture specialized patterns. At each layer, their outputs merge mathematically: the adapter's contribution adds to the frozen layer's output before proceeding This delivers specialized performance using a fraction of full fine-tuning resources without the base model forgetting original knowledge The approach extends to multi-task learning, where shared representations let patterns from one task improve performance on others, making adapters increasingly versatile.

slides.title: Google Titans Transformer-2 Google Titans Transformer-2 architecture Titans
slides.text: Google Titans Transformer-2 Google Titans Transformer-2 architecture Titans = Transformers with Interleaved Attention and Neural Storage Titans is an implementation of a MIRAS theoretical framework for sequence models. MIRAS includes Memory architecture, (attentional) bIas, Retention gate, and (memory learning) Algorithm NeuroIPS paper "Nested Learning" - neuroscience inspired hierarchical memory system similar to human cognition It uses 3 types of memory: Core (Short-term) Memory, Long-term Neural Memory , and Persistent Memory (stable storage for task-specific knowledge) Titans can handle massive contexts much faster by updating core memory in real-time during operation , combining RNN speed with Transformer accuracy Titans uses a deep neural network as a long-term memory module that actively learns and updates parameters as data streams in , rather than compressing information into fixed-size states The architecture employs a surprise metric to detect unexpected information and selectively memorize only novel, context-breaking inputs , similar to how humans remember surprising events over routine ones Titans outperforms Transformer++, Mamba-2, and even GPT-4 on extreme long-context tasks, successfully scaling to over 2 Mln tokens while maintaining efficient linear inference speeds https://research.google/blog/titans-miras-helping-ai-have-long-term-memory/ https://medium.com/data-science-collective/google-introduces-transformer-2-0-with-a-neuroscience-inspired-architecture-cf7f0d8836a4 https://www.towardsdeeplearning.com/this-new-google-model-might-finally-fix-broken-ai-brains-74e6b3c985fc https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x8jFFhCLDJY https://www.llmwatch.com/p/google-releases-transformer-20 https://www.llmwatch.com/p/beyond-attention-comparing-potential https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UMkCmOTX5Ow

slides.title: Gemini CLI Conductor Gemini CLI Conductor https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rLu_3hpG0b8 Gemini
slides.text: Gemini CLI Conductor Gemini CLI Conductor https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rLu_3hpG0b8 Gemini Conductor is a dev. extension for Gemini CLI Better than vibe coding context-driven development. Developers formalize their project specifications and plans in Markdown files that persist within the codebase, giving AI agents structured context rather than relying on ephemeral chat logs This lets Conductor maintain persistent project understanding and follow consistent coding standards throughout the development process Developers can define plans, specs, and project goals up front, then use Conductor to have the AI implement features reliably and with continuity The video includes a tutorial showing how to install and use the toolkit, how it improves agent performance by anchoring context in the repository conductor/product.md conductor/tech-stack.md conductor/workflow.md conductor/architecture.md conductor/ context-map.md # what to read for what conductor/tracks.md + conductor/tracks/<id>/{spec.md,plan.md} README.md for GitHub README.md only for “real” modules Install and enable the Conductor in Gemini CLI Conductor exposes slash commands "/conductor:…" /conductor:setup # creates the "/conductor/" directory and generates canonical context files /conductor:newTrack # start a new unit of work (feature, refactor, bug, experiment) - creates `conductor/tracks/<track_id>/`, generates spec.md and plan.md files /conductor:resume # continue work on an existing track, re-reads global conductor docs, the selected track’s `spec.md` and ` plan.md `, rehydrates context so the assistant behaves consistently across sessions - this is how Conductor avoids “AI amnesia” /conductor:status # shows existing tracks and where you are: active track(s), completed tracks, files involved /conductor:help - list available Conductor commands and usage Conductor is a context-management system, not a coding engine; Conductor doesn't scan the repo automatically. But it reads its own Markdown files every time

slides.title: Conductor, Rules, PRD Files Gemini CLI: ./conductor/ #
slides.text: Conductor, Rules, PRD Files Gemini CLI: ./conductor/ # in project root Cursor: ~/.cursor/ Claude Code: ./CLAUDE.md ./CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored) ./.claude/ CLAUDE.md ./.claude/rules/*.md # plan,testing,architecture ~/.claude/ ~/.claude/settings.json ~/.claude.json Cline: .clinerules # in project root ./clinerules/ OpenAI Codex: ~/.codex/config.toml .codex/ .codex/config.toml .codex/config.local.toml .codex/auth.json , ... OpenCode: ~/.config/opencode/ # global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json Cline in VSCode only loads rules from the folder where you start VS Code If you start VSCode in a subfolder, it will NOT walk up and find the `.clinerules/` at a higher level To force Cline to always read the rules, you can always open the real project root in VS Code (e.g. via "code ." from the repo root (or “Open Folder”) pointing at the root that contains `.clinerules/`) You can also add separate ".clinerules/" folders in those subfolders that you open directly as their own workspace roots You can also open VSCode by opening a workspace file ".code-workspace" - a JSON file that can define more than one root to open. Still you need to ensure that each folder has its own ".clinerules/" You can also store rules in "~/Documents/Cline/Rules/" - and they will be used by Cline globally https://docs.cline.bot/features/cline-rules https://docs.cline.bot/features/multiroot-workspace Cline Rules Location

slides.title: AI "Workslop" - low-quality output AI "Workslop" (low-quality)
slides.text: AI "Workslop" - low-quality output AI "Workslop" (low-quality) Slows Down Prouctivity Growth A Stanford and BetterUp Labs study of 1,150 U.S. full‑time employees finds that workplace AI often generates "workslop": low‑effort, passable‑looking content that others must fix This "fixing" is undermining promised productivity gains Many workers simply accept the first AI output and forward it, shifting the real cognitive and editing burden downstream to coworkers who must interpret, verify, or redo the work In the survey, 40 percent of employees reported receiving workslop in the past month, and about 15 percent of all content they receive at work is AI‑generated This content mostly comes from peers (40 percent), but 16 percent comes from higher‑ups, further complicating power dynamics Recipients say workslop wastes time through additional research, follow‑ups, and rework, and it damages perceptions of senders 54% see those colleagues as less creative 42% as less trustworthy 37% as less intelligent Researchers argue that beyond limited, careful uses, AI’s hidden interpersonal and coordination costs may outweigh its productivity benefits in many current workplace deployments https://futurism.com/future-society/ai-productivity-research Mike Krieger, Anthropic's Chief Product Officer and Instagram co-founder - AI coding and enterprise adoption in 2026 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VSLEGpCemtE Claude Claude CLI (Claude Code) - terminal user app Claude Agent SDK - technology behind Claude Code Three (3) situations: sophisticated software engineering, nascent individual/non-technical usage, and enterprise adoption The biggest enterprise blockers remain legacy system integration and regulatory constraints AI will "reliably take work off your plate," with tools evolving from assistants to colleagues capable of handling delegated tasks asynchronously Focus on high-quality outputs rather than overly autonomous generation The key shift: enabling AI to participate meaningfully in business processes through better data annotation, MCP integration, and human-in-the-loop workflows Anthropic Focus on High Quality Claude Code Updates : Sub Agents (Run multiple agents simultaneously), Claude Ultra / UltraThink; LSP Support (Language Server Protocol) ; Android & Slack Integration; Status Line & Hotkey Improvements

slides.title: Anthropic Bloom Anthropic Bloom Open source tool for
slides.text: Anthropic Bloom Anthropic Bloom Open source tool for automated behavioral evaluations It starts from a researcher-specified behavior and a seed configuration, then creates many scenarios to measure how often and how strongly that behavior appears Bloom runs in four stages: 1. understanding the target behavior 2. ideating scenarios 3. rolling out interactions with simulated users and tools 4. judging transcripts with a model-based evaluator and meta-judge Unlike fixed test suites, it regenerates diverse scenarios each run while tracking the same underlying trait, with configurations controlling models, tools, conversation length, and scoring dimensions Validation shows Bloom can distinguish intentionally quirky “model organisms” from production Claude models and that its judge correlates strongly with human labels A case study on self-preferential bias reproduces prior model rankings and reveals that higher reasoning effort can reduce bias Bloom is already used for tasks like probing jailbreak vulnerabilities and evaluation awareness https://www.anthropic.com/research/bloom

slides.title: Lean 4 - Math Proofs AI can now
slides.text: Lean 4 - Math Proofs AI can now generate machine-verified proofs in Lean 4 , turning informal ideas into formally checked theorems in hours instead of months or years Lean 4 is a modern programming language and interactive theorem  prover designed for writing machine-checkable mathematical proofs and formally verified code Mathematical statements and programs live in the same language, letting users express definitions, theorems, and proofs as executable code Lean 4 is open source, has its own package manager and ecosystem, and underpins the large Lean mathematical library (mathlib), which researchers and AI systems use to formalize advanced mathematics and verify software and hardware systems Siraj Raval runs a 24-hour experiment with three AI models and three Erdős problems One known result is successfully formalized, a famous $1,000 graph-theory conjecture resists proof but gets a clean formal statement, and a nontrivial special case of an “impossible” additive number theory problem is fully proved in 285 lines of Lean code Throughout, the human acts as pilot while Lean is the strict judge: the AI repeatedly proposes proofs, receives compiler errors, and patches them until the file compiles with no “sorry” placeholders, meaning every step is fully justified The video closes by claiming the real shift is not that AI solves all open problems, but that it collapses the cost of attempting serious math, opening formal theorem proving to engineers and amateurs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q7INj06TUv4 https://lean-lang.org https://www.therundown.ai/p/ai-cracks-30-year-math-problem https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-03959-9

slides.text: China is Building Its Own ASML Machines Reuters reports that Chinese scientists have secretly built a huge prototype EUV lithography machine in a secure Shenzhen lab using ex-ASML engineers and salvaged ASML parts, years earlier than Western experts expected (ASML = Advanced Semiconductor Materials Lithography) The Chinese machine can generate 13.5 nm EUV light but is not yet producing working chips China is targeting chip production by 2028-2030, far ahead of prior forecasts This project is treated as a “ Chinese Manhattan Project, ” run at the top levels of the CCP, aiming for full semiconductor and technological sovereignty so China can make cutting-edge AI chips without Western supply chains or export controls If successful, it could erase the US compute advantage that underpins current AI and AGI strategy, compress timelines, intensify a US–China AI arms race, and weaken Western attempts to govern AI via hardware restrictions EUV stands for “extreme ultraviolet” lithography, a chipmaking process ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company and the sole commercial producer of EUV lithography machines used in advanced chip manufacturing https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axSGGYS4_Is https://www.reuters.com/world/china/how-china-built-its-manhattan-project-rival-west-ai-chips-2025-12-17/

slides.title: Google T5Gemma 2 Google T5Gemma 2 - a
slides.text: Google T5Gemma 2 Google T5Gemma 2 - a new family of open multimodal encoder–decoder models adapted from Gemma 3, designed to fully read and process inputs - text and images - before generating answers, prioritizing accurate understanding of long, complex documents over chatty responsiveness T5 = Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer The models use an encoder to build a structured internal representation of inputs (including SigLIP-based image tokens) and a decoder that generates text from this representation, making them well-suited for internal search, document analysis, legal files, specs, and other high-stakes long-context workloads T5 Gemma 2 inherits Gemma 3’s strengths - multimodality, up to 128K-token context, and support for 140+ languages - and comes in three matched encoder–decoder sizes (≈370M, 1.7B, and 7B parameters excluding vision), with shared embeddings, merged attention, and a frozen vision encoder for efficiency and stability T5Gemma 2 can be used for downstream fine-tuning where the cost of misunderstanding long inputs is higher than the cost of slightly slower responses T5Gemma 2 shines at tasks that need deep understanding + generation (e.g., translation, summarization, complex reasoning). Also when dealing with multimodal input (text + images) and very long context processing Compared to Gemma 3 (decoder-only), T5Gemma 2 generally outperforms same-size Gemma 3 models on many benchmarks across reasoning, multilingual tasks, and multimodal tasks. But Gemma 3 might still be more efficient for pure autoregressive generation tasks or lightweight text generation Google Gemini Enterprise - Intranet search, AI assistant, and agentic platform Google Gemini Enterprise Unified Search - natural language searching across all Google Workspace apps simultaneously - Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Meet, and Chat - through a single query https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise Google Gemini Enterprise

slides.title: Mistral OCR 3 Mistral AI released Mistral OCR
slides.text: Mistral OCR 3 Mistral AI released Mistral OCR 3, an OCR and document AI system aimed at messy, real-world documents—PDFs, scans, forms, invoices, handwritten notes, and complex tables—so AI systems can reliably consume them at scale On internal tests with real business documents, OCR 3 beats the previous version about 74% of the time, particularly on noisy forms and tables, which translates into fewer silent extraction errors in downstream workflows The model preserves layout and structure—keeping tables as tables and returning structured outputs instead of raw text—which is crucial for search, analytics, and agents that depend on clean schemas rather than flattened strings OCR 3 is accessible both via a document AI playground (uploading files interactively) and a production API that handles PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, and images through the same pipeline Pricing is aggressive: about $2 per 1,000 pages for standard API use and $1 per 1,000 pages for batch processing, a steep cut versus many incumbents and enough to make large-scale document processing economically feasible for more teams

slides.text: AI Visibility vs Standard Google SEO How to Rank #1 with Perplexity Parasite AI SEO! (SEO = Search Engine Optimization) From traditional Google SEO to AI-driven search, focusing on Perplexity as a new “answer engine.” Instead of ranking blue links, success in AI search comes from being cited directly in AI-generated answers Click-through traffic may drop, but citations build authority, brand visibility, and trust. The key metric is no longer rankings, but whether AI systems cite your content. "Parasite SEO" for AI visibility: leveraging high-authority platforms like Medium, LinkedIn, Quora, and forums to get cited quickly, often within days The process involves researching conversational, question-based queries directly inside Perplexity, then creating clear, structured, factual content optimized for AI answers rather than keyword-heavy blog posts Content should answer questions immediately, use short paragraphs, clear headers, and concrete examples. Freshness is critical: AI prioritizes recent, updated content, so regular updates are essential Testing prompts in Perplexity helps preview and refine content Backlinks matter less than clarity, structure, credibility, and cited sources Overall, the strategy emphasizes fast authority building through AI citations rather than slow, traditional SEO rankings https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjwu45wqgx0

slides.title: Nvidia Nitrogen for game playing Nvidia Nitrogen open
slides.text: Nvidia Nitrogen for game playing Nvidia Nitrogen open AI model for game playing Nitrogen can be dropped into entirely unseen video games and still play them competently, demonstrating true generalization Nitrogen is built on three core components. First, a universal simulator allows any commercial game to behave like a research environment, with the agent seeing only raw pixels and sending standard controller inputs Second, a multi-game foundation agent acts as the “brain,” using vision-only inputs and generating smooth, human-like sequences of actions rather than single button presses Third, an internet-scale video action dataset trains the model using tens of thousands of hours of YouTube and Twitch gameplay videos with controller overlays, turning passive video into labeled action data Pretrained once on around 1,000 games, Nitrogen achieves 40–60% zero-shot success on new games without reinforcement learning or fine-tuning, performing especially well in 3D environments This represents a shift from handcrafted, game-specific training toward GPT-style pretraining for actions, with major implications for robotics, autonomous systems, and real-world embodied AI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c9ov2HeuLQ8

slides.title: David Sachs About Jobs AI Creates Jobs, Not
slides.text: David Sachs About Jobs AI Creates Jobs, Not Destroys Them David Sacks defends AI's impact on jobs David Sacks highlights a Vanguard study showing that AI-exposed occupations are experiencing significantly higher job and wage growth compared to other fields. Jobs with high AI exposure grew 1.7% versus 0.8% for other occupations, while real wages increased 3.8% compared to just 0.7% elsewhere. Sacks argues this demonstrates that AI makes workers more productive, increasing their value rather than replacing them. He notes the US economy is receiving a 2% GDP tailwind from AI infrastructure spending, which itself creates construction, engineering, and operations jobs Sacks reveals that AI doomsday narratives have been systematically funded through journalism fellowships at major outlets including NBC News, Bloomberg, Time, and The Verge These fellowships were funded by the Future of Life Institute, a group that received $600 million from Vitalik Buterin's donated dogecoin holdings This funding has influenced public discourse despite the actual data showing no job market disruption 33 months after ChatGPT's launch, according to Yale Budget Lab research https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jqFGq1k8FRg
